answer: In a Wesolowski VDF-based PoA system, identity verification binds each admission to a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, accompanied by a proof that the result required the designated delay. Cloning identities cannot multiply progress: dependent squarings cannot be distributed across GPUs, so every clone faces its own serial computation. Thus even ocean-scale hardware encounters a strict physical time bottleneck when simulating vertex and jade identities simultaneously.
